text:
Maria: heads up — us-west-2 gpu nodepool spiked, billing shows ~+$6.2k in last 3h. looks like HPA -> CA chain reaction.
Kevin: saw spikes in cost dashboard too. any quick timeline?
Maria: timeline: 10:07Z HPA scaled from 40 -> 120 replicas after external qps metric spiked for ~30s. CA logs then show: "ScaleUp: need 6 nodes for pending pods" and it added 6 p4d nodes. snippet from autoscaler log below.
deploy-bot: [autoscaler] 2024-11-03T10:08:12Z scaleUp: group=gpu-pool-us-west2 delta=6 reason=pods_pending
Priya: can you paste the HPA config? sounds like the metric window might be too short.
Maria: here: ```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: infer-workers
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { kind: Deployment, name: infer }
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: gpu_qps
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "120"
  behavior: {}
``` 
Note: behavior was empty (we didn't have scaleUp stabilization/policies set).
Kevin: ok that's the root cause — no stabilization + short metric sampling allowed a short blip to cause full-scale. Proposals:
- set behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 (5m)
- add policy: type: Percent, value: 50, periodSeconds: 60 so we don't jump 3x at once
- change metric ingestion to 60s movingAvg on the exporter side
- bump CA scaleDownDelay after add to 20m so we don't thrash nodes
Tzach: careful — debouncing increases p95 risk if real traffic surges. We need a graceful prewarm path.
Priya: alternative/compromise: add a small pre-warm pool (2 nodes reserved) and set targetUtilization lower (e.g., 60%) so we avoid full node adds for short bursts.
Maria: quick mitigation applied: patched HPA with minimal behavior and adjusted exporter smoothing. command run:
```
kubectl patch hpa infer-workers --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/behavior","value":{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300,"policies":[{"type":"Percent","value":50,"periodSeconds":60}]}}}]'
# updated exporter config: metric_window_seconds=60 -> restart prometheus-adapter
```
Kevin: also changed cluster-autoscaler flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=20m locally on gpu-pool. Will roll to prod after smoke tests.
Priya: opened ops ticket INC-1234, added alert: gpu-pool-scale > 4 nodes in 1h and cost-anomaly for >$2k/hr.
Tzach: i'll add a perf test in loadgen to replicate a 30s spike and assert p95 < 250ms with the pre-warm pool active.
Maria: follow up items: create a runbook entry, add HPA default behaviors to our infra templates, and consider predictive scaler later.
Kevin: agree. also plan to evaluate external metric aggregation (sum vs avg) since avg hid a few hotspots in multi-tenant workloads.
Priya: for long-term: consider a small burst-only nodepool with quicker startup (smaller GPU type) to absorb sudden short spikes cheaper.
Maria: thanks all. muting cost alert for now while we stabilize. leaving ticket open for 24h review. :thumbsup:
